prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a general method for constructing aryl amines.

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is the clearest case on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds. Aryl amines went from a narrow, harsh transformation to a routine, predictable one, with ligand design (bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphines) as the unifying logic. The evidence of adoption is what I trust most: it runs through pharmaceutical and agrochemical process chemistry, materials work and thousands of total syntheses, and it has had more than 25 years of independent confirmation. The attribution is also the cleanest I can find. Buchwald and Hartwig built the general, practical catalyst systems independently and in parallel, so a two-person prize needs no arbitrary cut. I see that as a better fit with the chemistry of molecule-making than the biology-adjacent candidates.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed cross-coupling will lead some colleagues to ask whether this is a second recognition of the same idea. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is on the credited list and Migita's is not, so priority is not completely tidy. The topic is also less obviously novel in concept than PROTACs or base editing: it extends a recognised reaction class by ligand engineering. If the committee wants a prize that opens a new field instead of perfecting a mature one, B069 is weaker.

responses.point: Zou ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first and photoredox second, calling the C-N work original beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize and photoredox a platform adopted in industry.
responses.response: I agree on B069 and on the Buchwald and Hartwig pairing. The 2010 prize rewarded C-C coupling with organometallic partners; amine coupling needed its own mechanistic and ligand solutions, notably the shift from tin amides to free amines with strong bases and bulky phosphines. On B054 I am less settled than Zou. The trio is arbitrary, since Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi have comparable claims, and MacMillan already has the 2021 prize. That is why I keep photoredox as an alternative rather than pairing it with B069.

responses.point: Aili ranks PROTACs and molecular glues first as event-driven pharmacology that makes undruggable targets accessible, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa credited.
responses.response: I accept that the modality is conceptually new, and I ranked it seventh only because I weigh maturity and the chemistry itself heavily. My reservations are specific. I know of no approved PROTAC, so the clinical payoff is still prospective. The credit is also split between two distinct strands, the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, with Sakamoto and Kim) and the cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito). A three-name cap forces us to cut either Ciulli and Gray or one whole strand. I would want that allocation settled before I could rank B045 above a mature method with clean credit.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as a game-changer with demonstrated real-world consequences, enabling siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines.
responses.response: The real-world impact is not in dispute, and I would not dismiss it as engineering. But I ask what was new chemically, and the answer is the ionizable-lipid pKa design principle, which is a real molecular insight. The prize-grade attribution is hard. Cullis, Hope and Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each contributed distinct elements (encapsulation, ionizable lipid design, lipidoid libraries), so I do not see a clean three-person group. I would sooner reward a transformation whose originators are unambiguous.

responses.point: Chabes ranks PROTACs first and genetic code expansion second, valuing original chemical solutions to biological constraints, with Schultz and Chin for B032.
responses.response: I share the instinct for original chemical solutions, and B032 is the biology-adjacent entry I rank highest because it is chemically designed: orthogonal pairs, new amino acid structures. My reservation is that much of the problem was solved by evolving synthetases, which is closer to biology than to bond construction. Lei Wang's early role also makes Schultz and Chin alone an incomplete attribution. It stays on my list of serious candidates but not as my first choice.

responses.point: Linke ranks dye-sensitised solar cells first, valuing a clear underlying principle in which a mesoscopic dye-sensitised TiO2 film separates light absorption from charge transport, with Gratzel and O'Regan credited.
responses.response: The principle is elegant and the 1991 paper is a clear anchor, so I understand the appeal. My concern is chemical rather than physical. The lasting value is in device engineering and charge-transport physics, with the dye chemistry a smaller part, and the commercial uptake has been far smaller than that of cross-coupling. Perovskites have also taken over the solar field. I would ask whether B018 will be remembered as the origin of a technology that mattered or as a landmark that was overtaken.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Priority between Kosugi (and Migita, who is not on the credited list) and Buchwald and Hartwig in 1994-1995.
Whether to pair B069 with a second distinct achievement, given the three-person cap and the MacMillan 2021 issue for B054.
Whether a PROTAC or molecular-glue allocation can be settled in a way that is not arbitrary.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or any other credited candidate, though as a synthetic organic chemist I am professionally close to the field of B069.
